questions.q: You studied engineering. Why do you want to join the civil services instead?
pointers: Honest, personal motivation (an incident or experience)
Link engineering skills to administration (problem-solving, data, projects)
Do not criticise your own field
One concrete example of public impact you want to create

questions.q: Name one big problem of your home district. How would you solve it as the District Magistrate?
pointers: Specific problem with a fact or number
Root cause, not just symptoms
2–3 practical steps using existing schemes
Convergence of departments and people's participation
How you would measure success

questions.q: Your hobby is reading. What was the last book you read and what did you learn from it?
pointers: Name a book you have actually read
One clear idea from it
Link the idea to governance or your life
Keep it short and genuine

questions.q: Should India move to simultaneous elections (One Nation, One Election)?
pointers: Arguments for: cost, governance continuity, less model-code disruption
Arguments against: federalism, constitutional changes, local issues getting lost
Mention the need for consensus
Balanced conclusion, not an extreme view

questions.q: Will AI replace government jobs? What should the government do?
pointers: AI changes tasks more than it removes all jobs
Opportunities: faster services, less corruption, better data
Risks: job loss, bias, privacy
Way forward: reskilling, human oversight, clear rules

questions.q: As SDM, a minister calls you to stop the demolition of an illegal building owned by his relative. What will you do?
pointers: Rule of law comes first
Polite but firm with the minister
Follow due process and record everything in writing
Inform seniors
No public confrontation, no favouritism

questions.q: You see your senior officer taking a bribe. What will you do?
pointers: Do not act on assumptions; be sure of the facts
Use the proper vigilance or complaint channel
Protect your own integrity, do not join in
Avoid public drama; stay professional

questions.q: Is coaching culture good or bad for UPSC aspirants?
pointers: Positives: guidance, structure, peer group
Negatives: cost, pressure, mental health, rote learning
Self-study and free resources are also enough for many
Balanced view with a suggestion

questions.q: As SP of a city, which three steps would you take first for women's safety?
pointers: Fast response: helplines, patrol, safe-route mapping
Prevention: lighting, CCTV, public transport checks
Trust: women help desks, sensitised police, quick FIRs
Community and school awareness

questions.q: You have not cleared this exam earlier. Why should we select you now?
pointers: Stay calm, do not sound defensive
What you learned from the failures
How you have grown (skills, maturity, work)
Confident, honest closing line

questions.q: Which is more important for India: economic growth or the environment?
pointers: It is not either-or: sustainable development
Examples: renewable energy, green jobs, clean air costs
Role of policy and technology
Clear, balanced conclusion

questions.q: If you are not selected this time, what will you do?
pointers: Honest Plan B, said calmly
Show you will still serve society in some way
No negativity or desperation
Positive, mature tone
